purpose: The ZebrafishEmbryoAnalyzer extension for 3D Slicer provides batch segmentation, body length, curvature classification, and eye/edema/swim bladder metrics for 2D zebrafish microscopy images using PyTorch-based neural network models.
summary: 🟢 Recommend merge. The ZebrafishEmbryoAnalyzer extension is exceptionally well-structured, follows Slicer scripted module conventions and best practices (such as lazy imports, robust MRML integration, proper cleanup of observers, and careful PyTorch integration via PyTorchUtils), includes a comprehensive test suite, and meets all safety, packaging, and licensing requirements.

safety.rationale: Inspected source code across all lib, core, and module files. No unsafe deserialization (torch models are loaded with proper manifest verification and caching), no command injection, no telemetry or unconsented data transmission, and network access is limited to explicit model downloads.

environment.rationale: Inspected CMakeLists.txt and dependency_installer.py. The extension declares PyTorch as a build dependency, utilizes the official PyTorchUtils extension for PyTorch installation without side effects or unasked downloads, avoids pinning numpy/scipy/vtk/etc., and installs dependencies cleanly.

packaging.rationale: Inspected CMakeLists.txt, ZebrafishEmbryoAnalyzer/CMakeLists.txt, and catalog entry. All imported Python modules are registered with slicerMacroBuildScriptedModule, dependencies match, and all listed files exist.

license.rationale: Inspected LICENSE file. Contains standard MIT license terms permitting distribution and use.

soundness.rationale: Inspected ZebrafishEmbryoAnalyzer.py, logic.py, mrml.py, and test files. Robust ScriptedLoadableModule architecture with proper observer cleanup, parameter node management, thread safety considerations, and comprehensive error handling.

utility.rationale: Inspected README.md, documentation images, and extensive test suite. Excellent documentation, comprehensive unit and integration tests, and clear usage guides.

not_checked: Executing code inside a live 3D Slicer session or running CTest suite (tests/ are present and extensive, but executed via static review of code and cmake configuration).
